Disappointing experience does not live up to the Michelin Guide standards, followed by defensive management.
Sep 2026 • Friends
I recently dined at La Fontaine French Bistrot and unfortunately found the overall experience, from food to service, falling well short of expectations.

- Long delays and poor pacing: We had to wait nearly an hour for our dishes to arrive. While other tables arriving after us were served promptly and nearly finished their meals, we were left waiting indefinitely. Acknowledging that the kitchen was busy does not excuse a broken dining rhythm (pacing). Complimentary water or a verbal apology cannot make up for a severely disrupted evening.
- Service discrepancies: Witnessing later-arriving guests receiving continuous service while our table waited endlessly points straight to a breakdown in order sequencing and floor coordination.

Regarding the restaurant's public response: Instead of genuinely taking accountability, management chose to write a lengthy justification arguing semantics about waiting times and denying operational flaws. Shifting the blame to "standard kitchen procedures" rather than addressing the core service failure shows a lack of true hospitality standards.

This review is shared constructively. I hope management focuses on tightening their operational workflows and treating customer feedback with actual empathy rather than defensive excuses.

A Creative Take on French Comfort Food
Aug 2026 • Solo
Grated Carrots, Fresh Goat Cheese & Soft-Boiled Egg — This dish was delicious and very well-balanced. The grated carrots almost made me feel like I was eating pasta, so I thought using them this way was creative. The goat cheese complemented the natural sweetness of the carrots and worked really well with the dressing. This is definitely something I would order again. My only wish was that the egg yolk had been runnier.

Traditional Veal Blanquette — The veal was tender and easy to cut, while the blanquette itself was creamy and the vegetables were cooked until soft. The accompanying riz pilaf was flavorful enough to enjoy on its own, and I appreciated that the portion was less than a cup since I didn’t want to eat too much rice that day. My main issue was that, despite the nice texture and tenderness of the veal, I found the blanquette itself quite bland. I wish it had a little more seasoning or depth of flavor.

Lemon Tart — The lemon tart was good. It wasn’t overly sweet and had a pleasant tanginess.

The servers were sweet and welcoming. I also really liked the restaurant’s design and atmosphere.

Authentic French Cuisine
Apr 2025 • Couples
Dining at this French restaurant was a delightful experience from start to finish. The beef tartare was simply outstanding — fresh, perfectly seasoned, and served with all the right accompaniments. It struck that perfect balance of richness and texture that’s hard to come by.

I was especially impressed by the bulot snails — tender, flavorful, and authentically French. It instantly brought back memories of quiet cafés in Paris. It’s rare to find this dish done so well outside of France, but they absolutely nailed it.

Beyond the food, the service truly stood out. The staff was warm, attentive, and professional without being overly formal. They made us feel welcome and comfortable, like regulars coming back to a familiar spot.

If you're looking for a genuine French culinary experience with heart, this place is a must-visit.

Perfectly executed French staples, somewhat better than Paris
Dec 2024 • Couples
In Vietnam there are well executed French cuisine by French trained Vietnamese chefs- and when they’re good food is technically perfect and taste is far superior to even very good places in France. We go all around france every year followed by trips to Vietnam and I really enjoy to discover really great Vietnamese chefs. Here the owners are French, I believe chef is French (or technically very well trained Viet) and the food is executed better than perfect. Exactly what you’d expect from an excellent bistro in France. My salmon was literally the best thing I had of its kind- skin perfectly crispy, portioned perfectly, leeks were creamy and divine, tomato with herbs also perfect balance. My husbands lamb pasta was also perfectly executed and seasoned and just delicious. Wine was great, dessert was good, tho I think pastry may not be their focus but still taste was very good. 10/10 can’t wait to go back.

Authentic French bistrot. Amazing food. Felt as if I was back in Poitiers. Highly recommended.
Apr 2024 • Couples
Finally, an authentic French bistrot that emphasises honest, rustic French flavours in a proper bistrot setting. La Fontaine is very diferent from the often over-priced 'fine dining' French restaurants in Saigon that prey on the ignorance about real French cuisine by local diners and tourists alike.

La Fontaine is a quintessentially relaxed bistrot but exceedingly high quality French cooking as you would find in Bordeaux, Poitiers or the side streets of Paris. The French owner/chef makes a personal effort to greet every guest in person and stops by the table to make recommendations ask about the food. The staff also exceptionally trained in French service style and offered to explain the menu, always attentive without being overbearing.

Prices are mid-range but certainly not overpriced like many other French places whilst maintaining really good quality standards (better quality ingredients then some of the 'fine dining' places I have been to. I really felt like i was back in Poitou-Charentes.

I also love the nod to being authentic with a full a la carte menu for lunch/dinner but also a more casual/'all day' menu of simple dishes and a French style 1st floor terrasse outside and a bistrot style bar to sit at during 'apero hour' (French happy hour) which is super super reasonably priced.

The interior look of the place is charming as if it was lifted directly from a French city street and placed in district 2 HCMC. They even have 11e Arrondisement 'Place de la Fontaine' Parisian street sign in the bistrot that adds to the charm.

In over 10 years in Saigon, the best French dining experience and to top it all off. Plenty of French speaking voices to be heard alongside English and Vietnamese speakers. A true sign of authenticity- the French dine there:)))))

Highly recommended! Vive la cuisine Francaise!!!!!

Authentic French Bistro Experience
Nov 2023 • Couples
Seated at the counter, on the terrasse or in the far-right corner of the recently opened La Fontaine French Bistrot either for a coffee, a business lunch or a romantic diner, I could be sitting in any number of French bistros in Paris. 

But it’s not just the white tablecloths, tiled floors, or the aroma of French onion soup that feel so familiar. It’s simply how you feel when you’re dining in La Fontaine.

Chef Thierry's passion for delivering an authentic all - day dining experience is evident in the restaurant's offerings. Whether dining inside or outside, you can expect impeccable service and a memorable “back
to essential” journey. 

Don’t forget to be happy 
🐼🐼

PS: For romantic couple, do not hesitate to book the table outside next to the fountain 🇫🇷
